**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?** It means that all the sacrifices and vision I held within were true all along. It’s a great addition to my journey and story.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?**Jiu-jitsu was my college

**What was your job before you started fighting?** I did security camera sales.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**I started training at age 20 while at Mississippi State University. I started because after finishing football, I didn’t want to just go home and lift weights and do nothing

else. I love to compete. I found a jiu-jitsu club at MSU and that’s where it all began.

**What ranks and titles have you held?**Three-stripe purple belt in jiu-jitsu and a brown belt in Muay Thai under Alan Belcher and Roufusport

**Do you have any heroes?**My grandpa was always my favorite person and hero. He taught me what it was like to be a man and how to be tough. He passed away from cancer in 2011.

**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?**It has been a dream on mine ever since I began fighting in 2010. I work with and coach people that are in the UFC and have seen more than a few of the fighters train and compete and I know that I am more than capable of competing with and beating them. I want fighting to be my life. I work at the gym now, but I want to be able to support myself off the money I make while showing the world how great I know I can be. Fighting on the local circuits, teaching classes and coaching pays the bills, but I want to do something that my son can be proud of as he grows up.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?**I earned my Athletic Training degree (Associates) from Itawamba Community College in MS. I also went to Mississippi State University, where I was earning my degree in Biological Sciences, but came up four classes short due to money.

**What was your job before you started fighting?**My first job was with Abercrombie & Fitch as a model (front of the store). I was a personal trainer at the gym at Itawamba Community College. I worked landscaping for five years while lifting weights at 3:30 in the morning and having to be at work at 5am until 4:30pm and then going straight to the gym until 9 to train every day. My last job before starting at Alan Belcher MMA Club was as a regional manager for a pulmonary company for two years.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**I started training because I saw Stallone, Jean-Claude Van Damme, Arnold Schwarzenegger and Jackie Chan movies. I thought it was cool and I wanted to learn to defend myself.

**What professional titles have you held?**LFA Light Heavyweight Champion and Jungle Fight Welterweight Champion

**Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines?** Jiu-Jitsu Black Belt

**Any belts/ ranks in striking disciplines?** Muay Thai Black Belt

**What fight do you consider to be the key fight of your career?**The next fight is always the most important. But the fight I had in Dana White's Contender Series, where I got into the UFC, was a very significant moment and one of the most important in my career.

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?**Jon Jones.What he did inside the octagon is incredible and unique.

**Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for?**To encourage people to pursue their goals in life and to show young people and teenagers that it is possible to achieve a dream through hard work.

**Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you?**The passion for fighting, facing challenges and the opportunity to win. And of course, being able to live off it and support my family doing what I love.  
  
**What was your job before you started fighting?**I've worked in a motorcycle workshop, I've been a horse farrier and currently I give private Muay Thai lessons

**Origin of nickname:** “My name is Bruno and I´m big”

**Personal Life / Background:**I have my wife, Luciana Fernandes, and my 3-year-old daughter, Stella. I also have a dog. I'm passionate about horses and, whenever I can, I go to the interior of São Paulo, in São Roque, to ride horses.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**I started MMA training in 2015, when the sport really began to take off in our country. What drew me in was the combination of wrestling, striking, and kicks. I had my first professional fight in 2017.

**What professional titles have you held?** Eagle FC light heavyweight champion.

**Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports?**I’m a world champion in pankration, a master of sports of international class in pankration, and a three-time Kazakhstan champion in hand-to-hand combat.

**What are your current ranks in martial arts?**I am an International Master of Sport in pankration, a Master of Sport in hand-to-hand combat, and also a Master of Sport in MMA.

**What has been your toughest fight to date and why?**My toughest fight was for the Eagle FC belt. Competing in front of my home crowd brought a lot of pressure, and I made some mistakes that could have been avoided. But I took valuable lessons from that fight, and I’ve grown into a much better fighter because of it.

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?**I wouldn’t say I have one favorite fighter, but there are athletes I grew up watching who inspired me to start training in mixed martial arts. Fighters like Fedor Emelianenko and Jon Jones—true masters of their craft. They were a big motivation for me to pursue this career.

**Beyond a championship and money, what motivates you?**My biggest motivation is my family. They always support me—in victories and in defeats. They are always by my side. That support is the foundation of my motivation.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?**Yes, I earned a bachelor’s degree in sports education.

**What was your job before you started fighting?**Before starting my professional fighting career, I worked as a loader, in a mine, and as a bodyguard.

**Personal Life / Background:**My life outside of fighting isn’t very flashy. Our job is training twice a day—morning and evening. Usually, once a week I spend time with my family. I have a wife and a daughter. On weekends, I like to be active—I enjoy playing football (soccer), and I often play on Saturdays in addition to my training. That helps me relax and recharge.

**What is one thing that you want UFC fans to know about you?**First of all, I want to raise the flag of my country and let people around the world know who the Kazakh people are and where Kazakhstan is. That’s very important to me. My previous fight ended in a loss, and this is my third fight under my contract. I’m extremely motivated and focused. God willing, I will deliver a spectacular and exciting performance for the fans.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**I was an elite athlete my entire upbringing (gymnast). After graduating from Baylor and becoming a 2x All-American in acro and tumbling, I needed to do more, so I started MMA.

**What ranks and titles have you held?**AKA amateur flyweight champ,Multi-time NAGA champ

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?**GSP is my forever favorite. I love how he utilized his athletic ability, was a true master of the mix of disciplines, and he always carried himself in and out of the cage to a very respectable standard.

**Do you have any heroes outside of fighting?**My parents! They are a perfect example of hard work and dedication. They have pointed my sisters and I to Jesus throughout life and I am beyond thankful for that. They pushed us hard growing up, but always made sure we knew how loved we were.

**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?**It means that every ounce of blood, sweat, and tears have paid off— and it means I am one step closer to the belt and the dream!

**What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why?**My Contender’s fight for sure. It was a great test against a great opponent under great stress.

**What are your current ranks in martial arts?**Black belt in Texas Redneck fighting

**Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you?**I’m motivated to succeed for everyone who has believed in me and who has poured into this dream of mine. The village I have is absolutely incredible and I want to do well for them— they have helped me and expected nothing to gain in return and I owe it to them as much as I owe it to me.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?**Baylor - Journalism - Public Relations / Marketing minor

**What was your job before you started fighting?**Student athlete (A&T for Baylor)

**Specific accomplishments in pro competition?**KO of the year nominee 2018,Top 10 female KOs

**Favorite grappling technique:** Head and arm choke or Kimura

**Favorite Striking technique:** Head kicks and knees to the head

**Tell us about your life outside of fighting:**I live on a little farm in Texas. My husband and I don’t have any kids yet but we have dogs! We love them to death! My hobbies are and forever will be giving back to the sport that built me— gymnastics. I still coach and always will. I also am very involved in church, both at home in Texas and in Las Vegas.

**Q&A**

**When and why did you start training for fighting?** I started training at the end of my senior year of college in 2017. I have always loved to watch boxing and MMA since I was a kid. When I was in college I wanted to improve as a football player and I saw that NFL players were training in various martial arts and with MMA coaches. Once I first stepped on the mats, I fell in love. I know I have been called to fight and it was for a purpose much greater than serving myself.

**What ranks and titles have you held?** Currently a white belt. No titles yet, but that will change.

**Do you have any heroes?** My parents. They came from The Democratic Republic of Congo and have shown me what it means to work hard and go after my dreams. They have amazing stories and inspired me to go after what I love.

**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?** It means that I get to do what I love for a living. I get a platform where I pray that I can be used by God to leave a positive impact on others’ lives daily. It will be affirmation that I have been called to fight. It will be the start of a legacy that can’t be taken away. One day when I have kids and a family of my own I can encourage them and others to go after what they are called to do and love.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?** Yes I have three. I have an associate’s degree in Business Administration and accounting, my Bachelor’s in Accounting and my Bachelor’s in Finance.

**What was your job before you started fighting**? I worked as an accountant, I bounced, and was a personal trainer.

**Favorite striking technique:** Turning elbow

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**I started training for my health and suddenly I saw myself doing very well and was encouraged by my instructors to pursue a career, so I made martial arts my life.

**What professional titles have you held?** Shooto Brazil Champion

**Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports?** No

**Any belts/ranks in grappling disciplines?** Jiu-Jitsu purple belt

**Any belts/ranks in striking disciplines?** Muay Thai black belt

**What has been your toughest fight to date and why?**My toughest fight was my debut at Shooto, I was very nervous because it was my first televised fight and my eye was hurt from an illegal blow. I thought I was going to be blinded but I was able to finish the fight with a lot of willpower, so, to me, that was the toughest fight of my career.

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?**Ilia Topuria because he’s got a firm game, he goes in there to do what needs to be done and executes it.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?**I started college for a Physical Education degree but I dropped out to dedicate myself to martial arts.

**What was your job before you started fighting?**I’ve worked as a waiter, management assistant, food delivery. I now work as a martial arts instructor.

**Personal Life / Background:**I’m single, my mother’s family lives in Maceio and my father lives with my brothers in Recife. I live alone in Rio de Janeiro.

**What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight?**I like to read the Bible, I go to church, I like to play video games, I watch Anime, walk my dog, ride my longboard skateboard, and go on hikes on trails with friends.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**Not many years ago, I used to go for some wrestling classes as a young kid but I was competing in K1 and Sanda as a junior. I have been training kickboxing since 2018. My MMA journey started in 2021. when I came to Family Fight Team.

**What does it mean for you to fight for the UFC?**Everything!I'm here to take over and put my name in the history of sport.

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?**Jon Jones, one and only; the spiritual energy that he brings to the cage is different.

**Do you have any heroes outside of fighting?**Novak Djokovic is the one I guess.

**What are your current ranks in martial arts?**I was Serbian amateur champion many years in row as a junior, Luta Livre Brown Belt

**Specific accomplishments in pro competition?**ARMMADA Heavyweight Champion, DWCS winner

**Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports?**As an amateur I was national champion of Sanda kickboxing for a couple of years and no one was really able to challenge me so I started my professional career quickly.

**What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why?**There are a couple of them that are specific to me but I would say that every fight that's coming up next is the most important one.

**Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for?**As I said, I'm here to put my first and last names in the history. To show the world what it means being a real Serbian.

**Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you?**My family is my biggest motivation, they won't be sad and hungry ever again as long as I am breathing.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?**I was going to college but stopped because I’m not a guy who can handle all this things at 1000% so I decided to go fully MMA

**Favorite grappling technique:**Arm Triangle, Electric Chair

**Favorite Striking technique:**Right Kick, Cross

**Tell us about your life outside of fighting:**I was born paralyzed by accident and a doctor's mistake but my parents did a good job and brought me back to normal after 2 years. Few years later my parents got divorced and I literally share all the memories with my younger brother who is also my favorite person, my biggest motivation.I'm chasing dreams and showing the world the power of Serbian blood. No kids yet, no special pets either. Outside of fighting I like to ride motorcycles,enjoy nature, play chess,sharpen my brain and be with family.

**What is one thing that you want UFC fans around the world to know about you?**Jovan Leka is just a proud Serbian kid that chases his dreams and legacy. Representing Serbia the way it should be represented. I will take my time and won't rush, but one thing is sure, I am going for that championship.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**I started training in 2012/2013 because I liked fighting and wrestling since I was a kid. I also started to lose weight and learn how to defend myself.

**What professional titles have you held?**Lux Fight League Bantamweight Champion

**Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports?**Champion in jiu-jitsu, grappling, and kickboxing tournaments

**Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines?** Brown Belt in BJJ

**What has been your toughest fight to date and why?**My third professional fight against a Brazilian. After the first round, I felt exhausted, like I couldn’t move my legs anymore. The guy was tough, but I still went out and fought through all three rounds. It was hard because I lacked experience, and that fight ended in a draw.

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?**Jon Jones, because when he fights, he does real MMA. He dominates in striking, wrestling, and jiu-jitsu.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?**Yes, I went, but I didn’t finish because I dedicated myself 100-percent to fighting.

**What was your job before you started fighting?**While I was studying, I had many part-time jobs: construction assistant, painting, kitchen work, waiter, kitchen helper, bartender, security guard — all to be able to keep training.

**Origin of nickname:**“Pegajoso” comes from the chubby ghost in Ghostbusters. The name stuck because I was also chubby when I started training, and I was good at jiu-jitsu, so they gave me that nickname.

**Who are 3 people you'd love to meet or work with?**I’d like to meet Jon Jones, Khabib Nurmagomedov, and Jason Statham.

**What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight?**I love eating and cooking, discovering new restaurants and cafes, going to the movies, running, swimming, and going to the forest or beach.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?** I started 9 years ago in Congo.

**Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports?** Amateur Boxing - Katanga Regional Champion.Two-time Amateur MMA Champion of Congo at Bantamweight 2020 and 2021. Never lost a round; all wins by knockout.

**What has been your toughest fight to date and why?** My fight against Gasmire Diatta at AKO 1, because Diatta has exceptional power and technique. He is the only one who has managed to survive up to the second round with me. Unfortunately for him, I knocked him out early in the 2nd.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?** No, my family did not have enough money.

**What was your job before you started fighting?**I was working as a mechanic’s assistant.

**Origin of nickname:** It's a name the crowd gave me when I was fighting in the Congo. People called me "sorcerer of the knockout" in Swahili (an African language). "The Knockout Wizard" is the English version.

**Background:** Not much. No kids, just training and fighting. I grew up in Congo all my life, trained there, and never left the country, except for fighting and coming back. I believe I will be the first guy training in a local Congolese gym to make it to the UFC. And I am coming there for the belts. I am happy to showcase my skills in front of the world.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**I started training in 2013 out of love for this sport.

**What professional titles have you held?** Rei da Selva Middleweight Champion

**Any belts/ranks in grappling disciplines?**Jiu-Jitsu black belt,dark blue level in Muay Thai.

**What fight do you consider the most important in your career so far and why?**The most important fight of my career was on the Contender Series. It would be very difficult to have another opportunity to enter the biggest organization in the world, the UFC.

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?** Jon Jones, because of his versatility.

**Do you have any heroes outside of fighting?**My hero is my mother. She raised me always trying to give me the best, even coming from a poor family. She has been my biggest motivation in my studies and now in my fighting career.

**Is there a cause you’d like to support using your platform?**I would like to support social work that helps underprivileged people through sports.

**Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you?**My biggest motivation is my family. I’m always working to change our reality.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?** Yes - Civil Engineering

**What was your job before you started fighting?** Engineering

**Personal Life/Background:**My life outside of fighting is centered around my family. I have three kids—Christian (12), Aysha (7), and Liz (1). I also have a pitbull named Arizona. My hobbies include being involved in sports with friends. I usually play soccer, footvolley, and get together to watch games and the UFC.

**What is one thing you want UFC fans around the world to know about you?**What I want them to know is that I’m a warrior who is constantly evolving, and I won’t stop until I reach the top. I still have a lot to improve, and I keep training to show what everyone expects to see inside the Octagon.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**I started when I was 15 years old; I thought I was born for this sport, and that I can achieve great things.

**What ranks and titles have you held?** Inka FC flyweight champ

**What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career?**The most important one was my Contender Series fight, because it was the door to entering the UFC, and it was against a tough opponent.

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?**Ilia Topuria and Dustin Poirier.

**Do you have any heroes outside of fighting?**Jesus Christ is my only hero.

**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?**It means I’ve reached one of my goals, and that I’ll be able to take care of my family – it’s a step closer to my ultimate goal of being UFC champion.

**Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for?**Yes. I want to use my platform to inspire young people who come from humble neighborhoods, like I do. I want to show that with discipline, consistency, and faith, dreams really can come true. A lot of times your environment tells you that you can’t make it, but I want to be proof that you can go far through hard work.

**Beyond a championship and money, what motivates you?**My family. I want money to stop being a problem. I want to support them — that’s why I do this.

**What was your job before you started fighting?** I worked in a pastry shop.

**Specific accomplishments in amateur competition:** Titan War FC champion.

**Specific accomplishments in professional competition:** Inka FC flyweight champ.

**Favorite grappling technique:** Rear naked choke

**Favorite striking technique:** Overhand right

**Tell us about your life outside of fighting:**I’m very much a homebody. I live in an apartment where I spend a lot of time playing video games and listening to music.

**What is one thing you want UFC Fans to know about you?**I want them to know that behind the fighter there’s a person who has faced fears, doubts, and difficult moments — but chose not to give up.If my journey can inspire someone to believe in themselves a little more, then I’m doing something right.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?** I originally started training to lose weight and stay in shape during the off-season in football back in high school. **What ranks and titles have you held?** I hold titles for Kauai cage match (170pro), Punishment in paradise amateur 185title, X1 amateur 185title, 808battlegrounds 185title, Nogi NAGA open expert division - 1st.

**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?** Fighting in the UFC means everything to me. Ever since I saw my first fight this is what I have been pursuing, and to get my name on that roster is the first of many goals I have for myself.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?**I started training at 15 years old, after having surgery for appendicitis. I got really skinny, and someone advised me to train. As soon as I started, I fell in love with the art, specially kickboxing.

**What professional titles have you held?**Brazilian Kickboxing Champion, No-Gi Jiu-Jitsu World Champion

**Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports?**3-time Kickboxing State Champion

**Any belts/ranks in grappling disciplines?** Blue belt in Jiu-Jitsu

**Any belts/ranks in striking disciplines?**Black belt in Kickboxing, Black belt in Muay Thai

**What has been your toughest fight to date and why?** Televised professional kickboxing match. I faced a very tough opponent with heavy hands, but I came out with the win

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?**Anderson Silva because of his unique fighting style

**What was your job before you started fighting?** Military paratrooper (Brazilian Army)

**Origin of nickname:** From being a military paratrooper (PQD = Paraquedista)

**Personal Life / Background (family stuff, kids, etc):** I have three brothers

**What are your hobbies, activities or other interests when not training for a fight?**I love being in nature, waterfalls, hiking, and flying kites

**When and why did you start training for fighting?** I grew up wrestling and playing baseball. As a teenager I found some UFC DVDs at a Blockbuster. I got hooked and found a small local gym. I trained sporadically while making a lot of bad decisions. When I’d had enough and wanted to change my life, I committed to fighting full-time.

**Training:** AM Practice: 2-3 hours of MMA or skill development. PM Recovery Session: Ice bath, Normatec, nutrition/hydration. PM Practice: BJJ, boxing, Muay Thai or S&C.

**What ranks and titles have you held?** Undefeated amateur champion.

**Do you have any heroes?** Anyone that works hard and accomplishes a goal that seems impossible.

**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?** To accomplish the goal that saved my life. I hope to set an example for people who are trying to change their life, too.

**What was your job before you started fighting?** I was a drug addict and a criminal. I never held a job before fighting. I worked construction and did personal training throughout most of my career, though.

**Q&A**

**When and why did you start training for fighting?** I started when I was in the Army. I was an Army Combatives instructor for three years.

**What ranks and titles have you held?** Black belt in Jiu-Jitsu. XFN bantamweight champion.

**Do you have any heroes?** All the men and women in uniform. If it wasn't for our soldiers defending this great country we would not be able to live in the amazing nation that we do.

**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?** It means everything to me. It means that all the years of blood, sweat, tears, sacrifice, and time away from my family had a meaning.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?** I started in Jiu-Jitsu very young at seven years old. I was taken by my father. My father is a black belt, my mother is a black belt and my brothers are black belts. I moved to MMA in 2014, and in 2015, I had my first MMA fight. I wanted to go to MMA because I always wanted to get the biggest achievements of my life, and from my first fight I always believed that I would make it to the biggest MMA event in the world. Even when I had a serious jaw injury and was having several people saying that I would not fight again, I proved the opposite so, for me, nothing else in this world terrifies me today. Only God knows what I suffered to be here.

**Training**:Wake up in the morning for physical training, in the afternoon, boxing training, and in the evening, Jiu Jitsu training.

**What ranks and titles have you held?** Invicta FC atomweight champion. I had many Jiu-Jitsu titles - I was Brazilian champion three times and I was world champion, and I also got a second place in the Long Beach Worlds

**Do you have any heroes?** Yes, all my family, my coaches and my followers who never gave up on me; to me, they are my heroes.

**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?** Fighting in the UFC is the reward of my life. I gave up everything to live this dream. I didn't have a social life, and my life is summarized as follows: from home to gym, from the gym to my home. I gave myself body and soul to this.

**Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?** Yes, I completed college in social work.

**What was your job before you started fighting?** I had a jiu-jitsu academy, and I taught and created a social project for children and teenagers. I closed the academy to focus only on MMA. I graduated, but I never wanted to practice my profession as a social worker; my love was always for fighting. I was always very competitive, I fought all the jiu-jitsu events, I went around the world fighting, and this is my true profession. It’s what I want for the rest of my life.

**Specific accomplishments in amateur competition?** In Jiu-Jitsu, I won the biggest titles - World and Brazilian of the IBJJF, CBJJ, CBJJE.

**Ranks in any martial arts styles:** Black belt in BJJ

**Favorite grappling technique:** Armlock

**What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?**Fighting in the UFC means everything to me; it’s a dream come true.

**When and why did you start training for fighting?** It started when I was eight years old because my parents fought a lot. I told myself that a man is never ever going to hit me; I'm going to learn to defend myself and I started training Karate at school.

**What professional titles have you held?** Champion of the 300 Sparta in Peru

**Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports?** International Taekwondo Champion, International Wushu Champion, National BJJ Champion and National Wrestling Champion

**Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines?** Blue belt in BJJ, blue belt in luta livre

**Any belts/ ranks in striking disciplines?** Black belt in taekwondo, Black belt in wushu

**What has been your toughest fight to date and why?** The hardest fight was for the title since it was a fight that I had already fought with that rival. The previous fight was a no contest, and this one had the pressure of the people and the title.

**Who is your favorite fighter and why?** Max Holloway, because his fights are bloody

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Yes, I studied international business administration but didn’t complete my degree due to my country situation

**What was your job before you started fighting?** I have been working since I was 12 years old. I have worked in everything and at 16 I already had my first business together with my best friend. At age 18, I had my cleaning chemical products company, and at 20, I migrated to another country.

**Personal Life / Background:** It was very hard for me to get here. I had a very complicated childhood, but I always knew how to cope with it in my own way. Since I was little, I kept myself very busy. I worked, trained, danced and studied. I always had my mind busy, my desires and my desire to grow and get ahead. They were above what I had experienced, and I’m grateful to my mother and father who always supported me in my sport. I had to leave my country, my fights, my studies, my company, my smiles to look for a future and that was very hard. I suffered, but I managed to advance, and when I was already at my best in my fights, my previous trainer, the one I trusted the most, betrayed me. He tried to abuse me and that took me out of fights for three years; I thought I would never do it. Today, I am here, one step away from my dreams. My advice to everyone is that no matter how many times you fall, the important thing is that you get up.

If I weren't a fighter, I would be an actress. I really like cameras, TV and I have participated in music videos and commercials such as a stuntman in Kia cars.
